probe_result: Pointer-local integrity and freshness are distinct. Digest/generation validation rejects mixed-field corruption and predecessor self-chaining rejects predecessor corruption, but both an atomic pair and an internally self-consistent chain accept a replayed older valid state. Reset/recreate-to-old and stale-old-valid are observationally equivalent to pointer-local validators. A freshness guarantee therefore needs a monotone witness outside the mutable pointer rollback domain; unreadable or incomplete witness state fails closed with no write.
mechanism_revision: Keep the canonical atomic generation+target-digest pointer, add predecessor-chain integrity, and separately require a trustworthy monotone generation floor reconstructed independently from immutable role-local generation evidence before authorizing recovered state. Self-consistency alone is not freshness evidence.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is conditional on a trustworthy external-to-pointer monotone floor and limited to one two-generation deterministic symbolic model with mixed-field corruption, predecessor corruption, reset/recreate to old-valid, stale-old-valid replay, and unreadable pointer. Safe floor reconstruction under partial listing, duplicate/forked certificates, whole-certificate-set rollback, repository history rewrite, GC, rate-limit partial listing, non-CAS stores, and external irreversible effects remains unresolved.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local durable state transport only
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: conditional logical result that integrity-only pointer recovery cannot certify freshness and floor-guarded self-chain rejects the tested old-valid replay when the floor is trustworthy
mechanism_assessment.unresolved_child: Test Chat-native monotone-floor reconstruction from immutable role-local generation certificates under partial listing, duplicate/forked certificates, unreadable newest certificate, and certificate-set rollback/truncation.

No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, protected-primary, hosted-compute, paid, finite-credit, manual-user, public-source, or scheduler semantics were used.
